thread:
mira: Heads up — spike in 502/504 for model-pulls from eu-west-1 around 10:02 UTC. Dashboard shows sudden TCP churn and connection resets. Suspect NAT egress port exhaustion on the AZ NATs.
alex: seeing same in traces, spikes in TIME_WAIT + conntrack entries. bucket of short TCP sessions from sidecars.
daniel: can you paste ss/conntrack samples?
mira: pasted a quick sample:```
# ss -s | head -n 10
Total: 150000 (kernel 120000)
TCP:   120000 (estab 300, closed 118000, orphaned 0, synrecv 0, timewait 112000/0)
Transport Total: 120000
# sudo cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count
98000
# sudo cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max
100000
```
sofia: that's basically saturated conntrack + TIME_WAIT avalanche. each NAT EIP only has ~64k ephemeral ports, with many in TIME_WAIT from short-lived HTTP->model pulls.
alex: also seeing 5xx upstream from edge-proxy: "dial tcp: connection reset by peer" in logs. that lines up with SNAT port exhaustion.
infra-lead: quick mitigation options: 1) add NAT GW per AZ (more EIPs) 2) add a pooled outbound proxy with connection reuse (sidecar pooling) 3) switch to NAT instances with source IP rotation 4) increase conntrack (temporary). Thoughts?
daniel: we can temporarily bump nf_conntrack_max to 250k in eu-west1 nodes, but that's just a bandaid; the root cause is port address space fragmentation per EIP.
sofia: agree. middle-term: add more NAT GW (or per-AZ additional EIP pool) and configure sidecar to reuse connections (keepalive). short-term do: rotate EIPs + bump conntrack + enable connection pooling on outbound proxy.
mira: quick runbook I followed:```
# rotate a new NAT gw (az-a)
aws ec2 allocate-address --domain vpc
aws ec2 create-nat-gateway --subnet-id subnet-xxx --allocation-id eipalloc-yyy
# check ports per EIP (approx)
# note: ephemeral ports ~ 32768-61000 or system default -> ~28k per IP unless adjusted
```
alex: should also verify kube-proxy mode — iptables can create many conntrack entries if pod-to-service hairpinning + external target. if we have sidecars creating short connections, connection reuse will reduce TIME_WAIT massively.
daniel: running a quick script to count distinct source ports seen by NAT:```
for eip in $(cat eips.txt); do aws logs filter-log-events --log-group-name nat-logs --filter-pattern "$eip" | jq -r '.events[].message' | awk '{print $7}' | sort -u | wc -l; done
```
mira: results: primary nat-a EIP used ~ 42k distinct ports, nat-b ~ 10k, nat-c ~ 3k — fragmentation from staggered EIP allocation + sticky flows.
infra-lead: action items: 1) infra to provision 2 extra NAT gateways (eu-west-1a, eu-west-1b) and attach new EIPs — infra-lead owns, ETA 30m 2) alex to enable sidecar connection pooling (keepalive + max idle conns) in canary pods, ETA 2h 3) daniel to bump nf_conntrack_max to 250k across nodes as temporary relief, ETA 15m 4) sofia to add alerting: track conntrack usage and per-NAT distinct port utilization, ETA 1h
alex: will also flip on long-lived connection proxy in green pool and route 10% traffic through it for canary. config snippet:```yaml
outboundProxy:
  keepalive: true
  maxIdleConns: 100
  maxIdleConnsPerHost: 20
```
sofia: note for SRE postmortem: include model-client retry/backoff tuning. aggressive retries create storm of short TCP connections.
daniel: bumped conntrack on one node for test: `sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=250000` — conntrack_count dropped below threshold after NAT rotation started.
mira: after provisioning extra NATs + rotating some routes to new EIPs, errors dropped ~85% over 10 minutes. dashboard: requests per second stable again. :tada: 
infra-lead: leaving this thread open until we've completed the followups and updated runbooks. I'll create a ticket for permanent solutions: egress proxy pooling + NAT autoscale + per-AZ EIP pool.
oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1045 — NAT port exhaustion, severity P2. Assigned: infra-lead.
sofia: will add a postmortem template and link to runbook once incident is closed.
mira: thanks all — will post final summary once runbook edits are in. :thumbsup:
